test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 02 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Choose the correct idiom for the word highlighted in bold.**
After working in the company for several years, Anita really knows the ropes** and can train new employees with ease.

options.text: To be skilled and experienced in a particular activity.
To be unaware of how something works.

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. To be skilled and experienced in a particular activity.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"knows the ropes"** refers to being skilled and experienced in a particular activity or job. (किसी गतिविधि या नौकरी में कुशल और अनुभवी होना) • **Example:** After working in the marketing industry for years, she knows the ropes and can handle any challenge. • This idiom is often used to describe people who have a deep understanding of how things work and are capable of training or guiding others. (यह मुहावरा अक्सर उन लोगों का वर्णन करने के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है जो चीजों को कैसे काम करते हैं, इसका गहरा ज्ञान रखते हैं।) • **Example:** The manager asked the senior employee to train the new hires since he knows the ropes. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. To be skilled and experienced in a particular activity.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 2: To be unaware of how something works** (कुछ काम करने के तरीके से अनजान होना) • **Example:** He is new to the team and doesn't know the ropes yet. • **Option 3: To be physically strong** (शारीरिक रूप से मजबूत होना) • **Example:** The athlete is physically strong and prepared for the competition. • **Option 4: To take unnecessary risks** (अनावश्यक जोखिम लेना) • **Example:** It's better to avoid taking unnecessary risks in business. bc:T911, The correct answer is '**has approved**'.
